evaluated.name: ProfitPerAccrualBloat
evaluated.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)
evaluated.hypothesis: Cumulative past accruals are embodied in the stock of net operating assets, so gross profit measured per dollar of accrual-accumulated operating capital separates firms that earn profits on a lean balance sheet from firms whose reported profits rest on a bloated receivable/inventory/net-operating-asset base that must eventually be written down.
evaluated.reasoning: Unlike a small additive perturbation of total assets, the deflator here is materially different — it strips cash and nets out operating liabilities — so the accrual channel drives large cross-sectional variation rather than acting cosmetically. It converts the accrual theme from a flow to a stock concept (balance-sheet bloat) and asks how much true trading profit that accrual stock supports, which is a distinct mechanism from period accruals.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CreditSignedProfitability
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), SIGN(NEG(DELTA(wcap, 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Reported operating profitability should be read as good news only when working capital is releasing cash; the same profitability level accompanied by a working-capital build is accrual-financed and mean-reverts, so the accrual sign should flip the interpretation of profits rather than merely shade it.
evaluated.reasoning: Because the profitability channel enters as a non-negative rank multiplied by a ±1 accrual sign, low-profitability firms are pushed toward zero regardless of accrual state and the extremes are populated only by highly profitable firms separated by cash backing — this is close to a pure interaction rather than a sum of main effects. Using wcap (a dedicated accruals variable) keeps coverage high relative to cash-flow-statement components.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ProfitVsAccrualBloatTrend
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), SIGN(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), at), 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Multi-year accumulation of net operating assets, not the single-year accrual flow, reveals whether a profitable firm is steadily capitalizing costs and stretching working capital; sustained profitability with a shrinking operating-asset base is genuinely cash-generative, while the same profitability with a rising base is accounting-driven and reverses.
evaluated.reasoning: Replacing the one-year accrual with a three-year trend in the accrual stock tests a slow-moving accounting-aggressiveness state that annual accrual flows measure noisily, while smoothing profitability with MA(·,3) matches the horizon of the credibility question. The sign-conditioning again concentrates the long and short legs among persistently profitable firms, so the spread is an accrual-quality bet, not a profitability bet.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AssetSideAccrualGrossProfit
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), SIGN(ADD(recch, invch)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Only asset-side accruals (receivables and inventory) indicate that reported margins were manufactured by shipping unsold or uncollected goods; payables and other liability-side items release cash for different reasons, so restricting the accrual conditioner to receivable and inventory changes should sharpen the credibility test on gross margins.
evaluated.reasoning: The cash-flow-statement components recch and invch measure the receivable/inventory drain directly rather than inferring it from balance-sheet differences contaminated by acquisitions and restatements, giving a cleaner conditioning variable for the "channel stuffing versus real demand" story. Contrasting this with Signal 1 tells us whether accrual composition or aggregate working-capital movement carries the interaction.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: StableWCAccrualProfitability
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), at), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Durable profitability requires a stable accrual process: firms with persistent operating profits whose working-capital accruals have low variance rely little on accounting discretion, so their profits are more informative about future cash flows than equally profitable firms with erratic accruals.
evaluated.reasoning: This repairs a design the critic accepted but the validator rejected, replacing the shared ib−oancf accrual with an accruals-exclusive working-capital accrual so the second-moment (Dechow–Dichev style) accounting-discretion channel can actually be tested. It is the only proposal in the batch using accrual *instability* rather than accrual level, sign, or trend, so it teaches a distinct lesson about which moment of the accrual process conditions profitability.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: EarningsToAccrualNoise
evaluated.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3), MA(ABS(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), at)), 5)), 1)
evaluated.hypothesis: Profitability is credible in proportion to how small the firm's habitual accrual adjustments are: a firm earning steady operating profits while its working capital barely moves is generating cash-validated earnings, whereas the same profit level accompanied by chronically large working-capital swings is largely an accounting-timing artifact that will reverse.
evaluated.reasoning: Rather than swapping a deflator on an existing profitability ratio, this makes the accrual channel the *scale of measurement error* in earnings, so the return premium is proportional to profitability divided by chronic accrual magnitude — a signal-to-noise construct with no published analogue in either the RNOA or Sloan families. Using mean absolute working-capital accruals over five years (not the current-year signed accrual) captures the firm's accounting style rather than one-year events, and winsorization controls the small-denominator tail.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AccrualGradedProfitability
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accrual intensity does not merely add to profitability information, it scales it: the higher a firm's profitability, the more its future returns depend on whether those profits were accompanied by large or small balance-sheet accruals, so the accrual measure should enter as a graded multiplier on the profitability signal.
evaluated.reasoning: The non-negative profitability rank multiplied by a mean-zero, industry-standardized accrual-quality score produces a pure interaction: unprofitable firms are compressed toward zero regardless of accruals, while the long and short tails are both highly profitable firms separated by accrual magnitude — so a positive result cannot be explained by either main effect alone. It also isolates one specific design choice against the accepted sign-conditioned signal: whether graded accrual intensity carries information beyond the mere sign of working-capital accruals.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashAdjProfitPerAccrualBloat
evaluated.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oibdp, SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1))), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)
evaluated.hypothesis: Durable profitability is cash operating profit — reported operating income minus the working-capital accrual that inflated it — measured per dollar of the accrual-accumulated operating capital that had to be tied up to earn it; both the flow and the stock of accruals must be charged against profits.
evaluated.reasoning: This keeps the deflator that produced the archive's best portfolio alpha but replaces the raw profit numerator with a materially cash-adjusted one (the accrual subtraction is comparable in size to the profit itself, unlike gen-0's trivial denominator perturbation), so the accrual channel now enters twice and in the same economic direction. It tests whether the GP/NOA result strengthens when the numerator is also purged of accrual content, which distinguishes the "accrual bloat" story from a plain profitability-per-capital story.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: GrossProfitGradedByBloat
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The reason profit-per-accrual-bloat works is an interaction, not a scaling convention: gross profitability is informative about future returns mainly for firms whose operating capital is lean, and nearly uninformative for firms whose balance sheet is inflated by accumulated accruals.
evaluated.reasoning: This decomposes the archive's best-alpha ratio into an explicit interaction between a non-negative profitability rank and an industry-standardized accrual-stock intensity, so the extremes are populated by profitable firms differing in balance-sheet bloat rather than by mechanical small-denominator cases. If the interaction form reproduces the ratio's alpha, we learn the effect is genuinely conditional; if it does not, the gen-0 result was a deflator effect and future work should stay in ratio space.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: LiabilityStretchGradedProfit
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(apalch, aoloch), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Not all cash backing is high quality: profitable firms whose operating cash flow is supported by stretching payables and other operating liabilities are financing themselves off suppliers rather than converting profits into cash, so their earnings are as fragile as those of receivable-builders.
evaluated.reasoning: Every prior proposal treated liability-side movements as improving accrual quality (they reduce Sloan accruals) whereas the economics of supplier financing suggest the opposite for profitable firms — this is a genuinely new channel and the first test of whether accrual quality is asymmetric across the asset and liability sides of working capital. Paired with Signal 4 it delivers a clean composition lesson rather than a repeated template.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: UnexpectedAccrualGradedProfit
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), MA(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 5)), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Only the *unexpected* part of accruals signals earnings that will reverse: a growing firm normally accrues working capital every year, so what discredits reported profits is an accrual this year far above the firm's own established accrual norm, which is the symptom of discretionary revenue pulling-forward rather than of business expansion.
evaluated.reasoning: Rather than rank-wrapping the archived signal, this changes the accrual construct itself from a cross-sectional level to a firm-specific abnormal-accrual deviation from a five-year norm, which is the standard discretionary-accrual identification idea and is economically distinct from Sloan-level accruals. The multiplier remains a signed industry z-score so the conditional sign-flip mechanism is preserved, and because abnormal accruals are far less persistent than accrual levels, the resulting portfolio should reshuffle on genuine accounting-quality news rather than on slow-moving firm characteristics — the plausible reason the level-graded version had a strong slope but a muted FF5 alpha.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CollectionBackedProfitMargin
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(recch, invch), sale), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Under the Compustat decrease-positive convention, positive RECCH+INVCH means receivables and inventory released cash, so profitable firms whose working capital is being collected and sold down have genuinely converted profits into cash, while equally profitable firms whose receivables and inventory absorb cash relative to sales are recognizing revenue ahead of collection and will reverse.
evaluated.reasoning: The direction is now set by the documented sign convention rather than by back-fitting to the earlier inverted t-stat, and if the archive's inversion was real it will show up here as a clean, interpretable rejection of the convention rather than as a hidden fudge. Deflating the receivable/inventory flow by sales rather than assets matches the channel-stuffing mechanism (working capital absorbed per dollar of revenue booked) and makes the conditioner comparable across capital intensities.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: DepreciationBackedProfit
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dpc, at), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that still earn strong profits *after* absorbing heavy non-cash depreciation charges are conservatively stated: their accrual accounting subtracts more from reported income than cash economics require, so their earnings are understated and more persistent than those of equally profitable firms carrying negligible non-cash charges.
evaluated.reasoning: Switching the profitability leg to post-depreciation operating income (oiadp) removes the internal inconsistency: the interaction now identifies firms whose profitability survives the conservative charge, not firms whose EBITDA is flattered by it. Industry standardization of dpc/at absorbs the bulk of the capital-intensity variation in D&A, leaving within-industry differences in depreciation aggressiveness as the conditioning variable, which is precisely the accrual-conservatism concept being tested.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashProfitPerWorkingCapital
evaluated.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oibdp, SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1))), SUB(act, che)), 1)
evaluated.hypothesis: Durable profitability is cash operating profit earned per dollar of non-cash working capital the firm must tie up; receivables and inventory are the accrual assets that both inflate reported profit and consume cash, so profit measured against that accrual stock separates real earning power from accounting-generated profit.
evaluated.reasoning: The best archive signal used a net-operating-asset deflator that can go negative for net-operating-liability firms, mechanically flipping the ratio's sign for a nontrivial subset; non-cash current assets are strictly non-negative, so this repairs the defect while keeping the cash-adjusted numerator that raised the alpha t-stat from 3.3 to 4.6. Excluding PPE also separates the "accrual bloat" story from the published net-operating-asset/asset-growth anomaly, which was the critic's main identification concern.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: TaxValidatedProfitability
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(pi, at)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(txp, at), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Earnings that create a real tax obligation have been validated by a third party with no incentive to accept accrual optimism; among equally profitable firms, those carrying substantial accrued taxes are reporting income the tax authority also recognizes, whereas high book profits with negligible tax accrual are book-only and reverse.
evaluated.reasoning: Book-tax conformity is an accrual-quality channel completely untested in the archive, and it is conceptually orthogonal to working-capital accruals because it constrains the *income* statement rather than the operating cycle. Pretax income is the correct profitability leg since it is the base on which the tax accrual is computed, making the interaction internally consistent in a way the earlier depreciation proposal was not.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ProfitVsExcessWCGrowth
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(GROWTH(SUB(act, che), 1), GROWTH(sale, 1)), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The right benchmark for accrual growth is sales growth: a profitable firm whose receivables and inventory grow faster than revenue is granting looser credit or accumulating unsold goods, so its profits are accrual-inflated, while a profitable firm whose working capital grows slower than sales is scaling on real demand.
evaluated.reasoning: All prior accrual conditioners were deflated by assets, which conflates efficient growth with accrual manipulation; benchmarking working-capital growth against sales growth removes the growth component and leaves the abnormal-accrual component, a normalization never tested in the archive. Because the conditioner is a growth differential rather than a level, it should also carry fresher information than the slow-moving bloat state while remaining economically the same credibility test.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ShortCycleProfitability
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Profits earned with a short (or negative) cash conversion cycle are the most credible: when customers pay before suppliers must be paid, reported profit converts into cash almost immediately and cannot have been manufactured by extending customer credit or stockpiling inventory, whereas the same profit earned with many days of working capital outstanding is accrual-dependent and reverts.
evaluated.reasoning: The conditioner is net operating working capital expressed in days of sales — a cash-conversion-cycle concept — rather than the one-year accrual flow whose sign the archive has already tested in both directions, so nothing about its outcome is implied by existing results. Deflating by sales instead of assets is also the economically right normalization for an operating-cycle length and separates the idea from the net-operating-asset/asset-growth family the critic flagged.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashRealizedProfitability
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(che, SUB(act, che)), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accrual quality shows up in the *composition* of the current asset base, not only in its flow: among equally profitable firms, those whose current assets have been realized into cash have collected their earnings, while those whose current assets sit in receivables and inventory hold profits that are still only accounting claims.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the rescaling exercise with a genuinely different accrual construct — the cash-versus-accrual mix of current assets, a stock-realization measure that no archive signal uses — while keeping the profitability leg bounded so both tails are populated by profitable firms differing in earnings realization. Because the conditioner is a within-current-asset composition ratio rather than an asset-scaled intensity, it is not a restatement of the accrual anomaly or of the NOA anomaly, and its cross-sectional distribution is far better behaved than the unbounded bloat z-score that produced the fmb/alpha divergence.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: PeakProfitAccrualRegime
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5), NEG(ZSCORE(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Profitability at a multi-year high is trustworthy only when the firm's working-capital intensity is simultaneously at a multi-year low; peak profits accompanied by historically elevated receivables and inventory are the classic signature of pulled-forward revenue and revert, while peak profits on a historically lean operating cycle reflect a genuine improvement in earning power.
evaluated.reasoning: Both legs are measured as positions in the firm's own five-year history, which is a regime concept absent from the archive (all prior signals used cross-sectional levels, one-year flows, or growth differentials) and which directly targets the reversal question the task poses. The profitability leg is a non-negative own-history percentile and the accrual leg a mean-zero cross-sectional standardization of an own-history percentile, so the extremes are firms at profitability peaks separated by whether their accrual intensity is also peaking — a true interaction with no single-ratio delta and no small-denominator differencing.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CumulativeAccrualGradedProfit
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(TS_SUM(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 5), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: What discredits a profitable firm is not the size of its operating asset base per se but how much of that base was built by accruals: five years of accumulated working-capital accruals measures the portion of the balance sheet created by accounting recognition rather than by capital investment, and profits resting on that accumulation are the ones that reverse.
evaluated.reasoning: This directly addresses the critic's concern that NOA-based conditioners reproduce the published net-operating-asset anomaly: cumulating the accrual flow isolates the accounting-created portion of operating capital while excluding the legitimate installed capital and initial endowment embedded in the NOA level. It also converts the flow family (strong slopes, weak alpha) into a slow-moving state without borrowing the NOA level itself, giving a clean test of which stock definition drives the alpha.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashAccumulationBackedProfit
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(che, 1), at), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The strongest evidence that reported profits are real is that the cash balance actually grew: profitable firms whose cash stock rises have collected their earnings, whereas equally profitable firms whose cash stock is flat or falling financed the reported profit with accruals or spent it maintaining the operating cycle.
evaluated.reasoning: Paired with Signal 3 this delivers a clean level-versus-flow lesson within the cash-realization channel — whether it is the accumulated cash position or the current-year cash build that certifies profits — which the archive has never tested. It is also economically distinct from working-capital accruals because cash accumulation is an outcome of the whole operating cycle, not a component of it.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ChronicAccrualGradedProfit
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 3), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Chronic accrual reliance, not a single year's accrual, is what marks profits as unsustainable: a firm that has expanded working capital faster than it collected cash for three consecutive years is systematically recognizing revenue ahead of cash, and its profitability should command no premium.
evaluated.reasoning: This repairs the archive's most consistent failure mode — flow-graded interactions with strong slopes (fmb 4.7) but negligible alpha (1.5%) — by converting the transient one-year accrual into a persistent three-year accounting-policy state that can sustain a stable long-short portfolio. If the alpha rises while the slope holds, we learn the flow family failed on portfolio persistence rather than on economics, which would redirect the remaining generations toward smoothed flow conditioners.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AbnormalWCDaysProfit
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale), MA(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale), 5)), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Every firm has a structural working-capital cycle determined by its industry and business model; what discredits reported profits is a stretch in receivable and inventory days *relative to the firm's own established cycle*, because that deviation cannot be explained by the operating model and must reflect looser credit terms or unsold output.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a new conditioning construct rather than a blend: it measures the accrual state as a stock in days of sales (the family that has produced the archive's tradable alphas) but benchmarks it against the firm's own five-year norm (the normalization that has produced the archive's strongest Fama-MacBeth slopes), which is precisely the combination the evidence says is missing. Because the deviation is firm-centered, it also avoids the cross-sectional industry tilt that makes level-based bloat conditioners resemble the published net-operating-asset anomaly.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CumulativeCashBuildProfit
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(DELTA(che, 1), 5), at), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Over a full business cycle, genuine profits must eventually show up in the cash box: a firm reporting sustained profitability whose cash balance has accumulated over five years has converted earnings into settled cash, while a persistently "profitable" firm whose cumulative cash build is nil has recycled its reported earnings into accrual assets.
evaluated.reasoning: This is not a rescaling of the current-asset composition ratio — it is a multi-year cumulative flow, so it distinguishes firms that were always cash-rich (a static balance-sheet type) from firms that actually built cash out of the profits they reported, which is the economically relevant validation. Paired with the accepted one-year cash-build signal it delivers a genuine horizon lesson: whether profit certification requires a single year's cash accretion or a sustained multi-year record.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: WeakestLinkQualityProfit
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Earnings credibility is conjunctive, not additive: a firm qualifies as durably profitable only if it clears both hurdles — high profit per dollar of accrual-accumulated capital *and* no current-year accrual inflation — and failing either one is sufficient to make its profits suspect, regardless of how strong the other looks.
evaluated.reasoning: A minimum of two industry ranks is a weakest-link aggregation that no archive signal uses and that behaves nothing like an ensemble: averaging lets a strong accrual score rescue weak bloat-adjusted profitability, whereas MIN does not, so the long leg contains only firms credible on both dimensions and the result identifies whether the market prices joint credibility rather than either component. Both inputs are bounded industry percentiles, which should keep the Fama-MacBeth slope and the decile spread reading the same ordering — the divergence that has plagued the unbounded product designs.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: TripleHurdleQualityProfit
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 3), 1))), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che, act), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Durable profitability requires clearing three independent credibility hurdles — high profit per dollar of accrual-accumulated capital, no chronic multi-year accrual reliance, and current assets actually realized into cash — and firms failing any one of them hold earnings that will reverse.
evaluated.reasoning: Each added hurdle is drawn from an independently validated channel (bloat ratio alpha 4.1%, chronic accrual state alpha 3.4% with Sharpe 0.40, cash realization alpha 5.4%), and because MIN is conjunctive rather than averaging, the third screen removes firms that pass on two dimensions rather than diluting them, which is not achievable by blending. The risk is that a triple minimum concentrates the long leg too narrowly, so the diagnostic value lies in comparing its Sharpe and alpha t-stat against the two-hurdle version.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: WeakestLinkCashRealization
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che, act), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The two strongest forms of accrual validation are structural (profit earned per dollar of accrual-bloated capital) and realizational (current assets converted into cash); a firm must satisfy both, because capital-efficient profits held entirely in receivables are as suspect as cash-rich firms with no earning power.
evaluated.reasoning: This substitutes the accrual *stock realization* channel for the accrual *flow* channel inside the winning conjunctive structure, testing whether the weakest-link result depends on the specific flow measure or generalizes across accrual concepts. Because the cash-realization channel previously delivered a 5.4% alpha with a wrong-signed slope, embedding it in bounded ranks also tests whether conjunctive rank construction repairs that divergence.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: WeakestLinkPlainProfit
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: If conjunctive screening is what matters, then requiring plain operating profitability and clean accruals jointly should already capture most of the effect, and the accrual-bloat deflator in the profitability leg is a refinement rather than the source of the result.
evaluated.reasoning: This decomposes the archive's best signal by stripping the NOA deflator from the profitability hurdle while keeping the conjunctive structure and the accrual hurdle intact, which separates "profitability measured against accrual capital" from "profitability screened by accrual quality." The comparison is essential for interpretation: if performance is preserved, the mechanism is joint credibility screening; if it collapses, the accrual-stock deflator is doing the work and later refinements should target the deflator.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashBackingConsistencyProfit
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_ZSCORE(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at)), 0), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Consistency of cash backing, not its average magnitude, certifies profits: a firm that has released rather than absorbed working capital in most of the last five years has demonstrated a repeatable cash-generative operating model, whereas the same average accrual achieved through one large swing reveals nothing about durability.
evaluated.reasoning: A count of cash-backed years is a genuinely new accrual construct here — it is invariant to accrual magnitude and therefore immune to the outlier-driven skew that produced the archive's fmb/alpha divergences, and it distinguishes persistence from average level, which the three- and five-year accrual averages cannot. It also tests the durability hypothesis in its most literal form, asking whether the market underprices a repeated record of converting profits into cash.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: MarginTurnoverWeakestLink
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(sale, SUB(act, che)), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Credible profitability requires both a high margin on what is sold and rapid turnover of the accrual assets used to sell it: a fat margin combined with slow-moving receivables and inventory means revenue is being booked faster than goods move and cash arrives, while fast working-capital turnover on a thin margin is volume without earning power.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a new economic decomposition rather than an aggregation swap — it splits profitability into the margin dimension and makes the accrual dimension the *turnover velocity of accrual assets*, a quantity no archive signal has used, so neither leg is one of the published anomalies the critic identified. Both legs are bounded industry percentiles and jointly required, the structure that just produced the archive's only signal strong on the cross-sectional slope, the FF5 alpha, and the Sharpe simultaneously.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AbnormalCycleWeakestLink
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale), MA(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale), 5)), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A firm's profits are durable only if it is efficient in the cross-section *and* undistorted relative to its own history: high profit per dollar of accrual capital certifies the business model, while receivable and inventory days no higher than the firm's own five-year norm certifies that this year's earnings were not manufactured by stretching that model.
evaluated.reasoning: The two hurdles draw on orthogonal information sets — one cross-sectional and structural, the other firm-centered and time-series — so unlike a pairing of two cross-sectional anomalies this conjunction cannot be a relabeled rank-average of gross profitability and Sloan accruals. Both components have independently delivered alpha with Sharpe near 0.4 (bloat ratio and abnormal working-capital days), and imposing them jointly should raise the alpha t-stat rather than dilute it, which is why this is submitted as a candidate improvement rather than a diagnostic.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: PersistentJointCredibility
evaluated.expression: TS_MIN(MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 1)))), 3)
evaluated.hypothesis: Durable profitability means never having failed the credibility test: a firm whose worst joint score over the last three years is still high has been capital-efficient and accrual-clean every year, whereas a firm that clears both hurdles only in the current year may simply be between accrual reversals.
evaluated.reasoning: This applies the weakest-link logic in a second, orthogonal direction — across time rather than across dimensions — which is a genuinely new construct rather than another channel substitution, and it directly targets the task's durability question by penalizing firms whose credibility is episodic. Because a time-series minimum of a bounded percentile is itself bounded and slow-moving, it should raise portfolio stability and Sharpe relative to the single-year conjunction, whose 0.545 is already the archive high.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ConsistencyHurdleQuality
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at)), 0), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The frequency with which a firm releases rather than absorbs working capital is a magnitude-invariant measure of cash backing, and profits are durable only when high capital efficiency is combined with a repeated record of cash-backed years.
evaluated.reasoning: This repairs the archived consistency signal's structural flaw — multiplying a profitability rank by a signed industry z-score inverts the ordering in the low-consistency tail, which is exactly the pathology that produced perverse results in several earlier conditional designs — by re-expressing consistency as a hurdle inside the conjunction. The count is immune to accrual outliers, so if it performs comparably to the winsorized flow hurdle we learn that the priced content of accruals is their sign frequency rather than their magnitude.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashProfitChronicAccrualHurdle
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oibdp, SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1))), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 3), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The strongest form of the credibility test uses cash-adjusted profit per dollar of accrual capital as the profitability hurdle and chronic multi-year accrual reliance as the accounting hurdle, so that neither a single clean year nor an accrual-inflated profit level can qualify a firm.
evaluated.reasoning: Both leg upgrades are independently validated — the cash-adjusted numerator lifted the ratio family's Sharpe to 0.448 and the chronic three-year accrual state lifted the graded family's alpha from 1.5% to 3.4% with Sharpe 0.40 — so combining them inside the conjunctive structure tests whether the refinements are complementary or redundant. Using a smoothed accrual hurdle alongside a cash-adjusted numerator also avoids double-counting the same single-year accrual in both legs, which the current-flow version would do.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashBuildHurdleQuality
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(DELTA(che, 1), 5), at), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Profits are fully validated only when capital-efficient operations are matched by an actual multi-year accumulation of cash, since a firm can look lean on the balance sheet while never converting its reported earnings into a growing cash balance.
evaluated.reasoning: The five-year cash-build channel produced the archive's second-highest alpha (4.3%, t 4.99) but a zero Fama-MacBeth slope, the classic symptom of an unbounded, skewed multiplier; embedding it as a bounded rank hurdle is the specific repair the bounded-rank evidence prescribes, and it tests whether the alpha survives when the ordering is made regression-readable. It also brings a validation channel independent of working-capital accounting into the conjunctive family, which so far relies almost entirely on working-capital constructs.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: DuPontAccrualTripleHurdle
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale)), MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(sale, SUB(act, che)), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 1)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Credible earnings require margin, velocity, and clean accounting simultaneously: a fat margin certifies pricing power, rapid turnover of receivables and inventory certifies that goods actually move and cash actually arrives, and a small working-capital accrual certifies that this year's profit was not created by relaxing either discipline.
evaluated.reasoning: This decomposes the winning profit-per-accrual-capital ratio into its economically interpretable margin and accrual-asset-velocity components and adds the accrual hurdle, so a strong result identifies which component of capital efficiency the market misprices rather than treating the ratio as a black box. The margin-times-velocity conjunction already delivered fmb 4.39 and alpha 3.1% on its own, so the incremental question is whether the accrual screen adds independent credibility information to a purely operational pair.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: IntangibleAdjustedQualityHurdle
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(revt, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accrual accounting distorts profitability in two opposite directions: working-capital accruals inflate reported profits, while the mandatory expensing of R&D deflates them, so the credibility test should compare accrual-clean earnings against a profitability measure that restores the investment accounting understates — R&D-inclusive profit per dollar of accrual-accumulated operating capital.
evaluated.reasoning: This changes the economic content of the profitability hurdle rather than intersecting two archived winners: every conjunctive signal so far has used unadjusted gross profit or EBITDA, which systematically ranks research-intensive firms as unprofitable even when their accruals are clean and their capital base is lean, so the long leg has been excluding a set of firms the hypothesis says should qualify. Treating unreported R&D as zero is the economically correct convention (firms that do not report the item do not spend on it), and the accrual hurdle is left untouched so the test attributes any improvement specifically to correcting conservative intangible accounting inside the profitability leg.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: IntangibleCapitalQualityHurdle
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(revt, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Consistent intangible accounting requires adding expensed R&D back to profit *and* recognizing the R&D capital stock it created in the denominator; otherwise research-intensive firms are flattered by an artificially small capital base, and the profitability hurdle measures accounting treatment rather than earning power.
evaluated.reasoning: The numerator-only R&D add-back produced the archive's best cross-sectional slope (6.32) but no alpha gain, which is the signature of a correctly ordered signal whose extreme long leg is contaminated by firms that look efficient only because their intangible investment is unbooked; capitalizing five years of R&D in the denominator removes exactly that contamination. It keeps the two-hurdle structure and the validated accrual hurdle untouched, so any alpha improvement is attributable to the capital-base correction.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: TotalAccrualHurdleQuality
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), dp), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Total accruals — working-capital accruals net of depreciation — are the complete measure of the non-cash component of earnings, so for capital-intensive firms the credibility hurdle should credit the conservative non-cash charge that working-capital accruals alone ignore.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive's conjunctive family uses only the working-capital component, which systematically flags heavily depreciating firms as accrual-clean regardless of their revenue-recognition behavior and mis-ranks asset-light firms in the opposite direction; including depreciation makes the hurdle the accounting-complete non-cash share of profit. This is the one accrual-definition dimension never varied inside the winning structure, and it directly tests whether the priced content is working-capital manipulation specifically or non-cash earnings generally.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AccrualStabilityHurdleQuality
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(VOL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 1), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accrual *instability* is an accounting-discretion proxy: a capital-efficient firm whose accruals swing widely from year to year is relying on estimation latitude, so its profits are less informative about future cash flows than those of an equally efficient firm with a smooth accrual process.
evaluated.reasoning: This repairs a documented failure — the same economics implemented as a product with a signed multiplier delivered alpha −2.3% (t −2.6) in gen 1 — and the archive has since shown that the failure mode was the multiplicative signed structure, not the discretion channel, because recasting other inverted conditioners as bounded hurdles restored them. It is also the only second-moment hurdle in the conjunctive family, so it tests whether credibility depends on the level of accruals or on the reliability of the accrual process.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: WorstYearAccrualHurdle
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(TS_MAX(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 1), 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accrual credibility is broken by spikes, not by averages: a single year of aggressive working-capital build-up reveals that management will use accrual latitude when needed, and the associated reversal is still working through earnings, so the relevant hurdle is the firm's worst accrual year over the recent past rather than its mean.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a tail-based accrual construct that is genuinely different from the archive's level, three-year mean, five-year sum, and sign-frequency hurdles, and it is asymmetric where accrual volatility is symmetric — it penalizes only upward spikes while continuing to reward large working-capital releases, which the volatility hurdle in Signal 4 would penalize. Comparing the two identifies whether the market punishes accrual uncertainty per se or specifically the reversal risk created by aggressive years, which is the sharpest remaining question about how accrual quality separates durable from reversing profits.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: SelfFundedAccrualBaseQuality
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, SUB(act, che)), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accrual quality has a financing dimension the archive has never tested: profits earned on a receivable-and-inventory base funded by short-term debt are fragile, because the accrual assets must be refinanced before they convert to cash, whereas the same profits on a self-funded accrual base survive a funding squeeze and do not force fire-sale write-downs of inventory or receivables.
evaluated.reasoning: This introduces genuinely new economic content into the conjunctive family — how the accrual stock is financed, rather than how large it is, how fast it grows, or how variable it is — using an accruals-menu variable (dlc) that no prior signal has employed. It also gives an independent reason why accrual-heavy profitable firms underperform (refinancing-contingent reversals rather than pure revenue-recognition reversal), so the result discriminates between two distinct explanations of the same archived spread.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ConservativeChargeHurdleQuality
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oiadp, SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(dpc, at), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that remain highly profitable per dollar of accrual capital *after* absorbing heavy non-cash depreciation and amortization charges are reporting conservatively: their accrual accounting subtracts more from income than cash economics require, so their earnings understate durable cash flow and are underpriced.
evaluated.reasoning: The conservatism channel produced one of the archive's strongest cross-sectional slopes (fmb 4.76) but essentially no alpha (0.5%) when implemented as a signed multiplicative z-score, and the archive has repeatedly shown that recasting such channels as bounded rank hurdles inside the conjunction converts slope-only evidence into tradable alpha (the cash-build channel went from a zero slope to 4.0% alpha at t 4.5 under exactly this repair). Measuring profitability after depreciation makes the interaction internally consistent — it identifies firms whose profits survive the conservative charge — which is the specific defect the critic identified in the original conservatism proposal.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: SupplierFinancedCycleQuality
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), SUB(act, che)), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Trade credit received is evidence of bargaining power and of a genuinely cash-generative operating cycle: a profitable firm whose receivables and inventory are largely financed by suppliers rather than by its own capital is collecting before it pays, so its profits are cash-backed by construction, whereas a firm carrying its accrual base on its own balance sheet must wait for the cycle to close.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive established the direction empirically — penalizing operating-liability expansion produced alpha −4.1% (t −2.7), implying liability-side accruals carry the conventional sign — and the complementary short-term-debt version of this financing idea worked as a hurdle (fmb 4.36, alpha 3.8%), but the stock of supplier financing relative to the accrual base it funds has never been tested. It measures a structural competitive-position feature rather than a one-year flow, which is the property that has distinguished the archive's high-Sharpe hurdles from its transient ones.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashFlowStatementAccrualHurdle
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(recch, ADD(invch, apalch)), at), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Working-capital accruals measured directly from the cash-flow statement are free of the acquisition, divestiture, and currency-translation artifacts that contaminate balance-sheet differences, so the credibility hurdle built from reported receivable, inventory and payable cash flows should separate durable from reversing profits more sharply than the balance-sheet accrual.
evaluated.reasoning: Gens 1–2 produced contradictory evidence on these fields (sign-based fmb −2.17, graded fmb +2.04), leaving the measurement question unresolved; embedding them as a bounded hurdle in the structure that has produced consistent results across every other accrual definition is the cleanest available resolution, with the documented decrease-positive convention fixing the sign a priori. The known cost is coverage (cash-flow-statement items bind at roughly 0.08 versus 0.11), so the result should be judged on alpha t-stat and Sharpe rather than on magnitude alone.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: GrowthAdjustedAccrualHurdle
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), MUL(GROWTH(sale, 1), RATIO(LAG(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at))), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A growing firm must accrue working capital simply to support its larger sales base, so the credibility hurdle should penalize only the accrual in excess of what the firm's own revenue growth mechanically requires — the residual after subtracting last year's working-capital base scaled up by this year's sales growth is the discretionary part that reverses.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the raw accrual hurdle with a firm-specific expected-accrual benchmark built from the firm's own prior working-capital intensity and realized sales growth, which is new economic content rather than a recombination of two archived legs: every hurdle tested so far penalizes the accrual level, mean, spike, or volatility, none nets out the accrual that growth requires. It should raise both statistics by moving fast-growing but honestly-accruing firms out of the short leg and leaving only discretionary accruers there, which is exactly the population the reversal hypothesis targets.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ProfitFloorAccrualHurdle
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(TS_MIN(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Durable earning power is best evidenced by a floor rather than a level: a firm whose *worst* year of profit per accrual dollar over the last three years is still high has demonstrated that its capital efficiency does not depend on favorable conditions, and combining that floor with current accrual cleanliness identifies profits that are both structurally earned and honestly reported.
evaluated.reasoning: The tail concept is moved from the accrual hurdle to the profitability hurdle, which is new content: the archive has tested worst-case accruals but never a worst-case profitability floor, and unlike the archived time-minimum of the joint score this keeps the accrual screen contemporaneous so the signal responds to current accounting news while the profitability requirement is structural. That separation also avoids the correlation problem that made the fully time-minimized conjunction weaker than the single-year version.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AssetSideRecognitionHurdle
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), sale), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Revenue recognition is an asset-side act: profits are pulled forward by booking receivables and building inventory, not by managing payables, so the hurdle that screens recognition aggressiveness should measure the increase in non-cash current assets per dollar of revenue and should exclude both the payables offset and the depreciation charge, which reflect financing and capital intensity rather than recognition.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a different economic object from every accrual hurdle in the archive, all of which net operating liabilities against operating assets and thereby let a payables build-up mask a receivable and inventory build-up of the same size; isolating the asset side makes the hurdle a clean revenue-recognition screen and removes the depreciation-to-sales capital-intensity contamination the critic identified. Scaling by sales is now internally consistent, since both numerator and denominator refer to the same recognition decision.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AccrualShareOfProfitMagnitude
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), dp), 5), TS_SUM(ABS(oibdp), 5)), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accrual reliance should be judged against the size of the profits it purports to measure: cumulative five-year accruals expressed per dollar of cumulative absolute operating profit measures how much of a firm's reported earning power over a business cycle was accounting recognition rather than cash, and profits with a low accrual share persist.
evaluated.reasoning: Deflating by the five-year sum of *absolute* operating profit removes the sign-inversion defect the critic identified — the denominator is strictly positive, so weak and loss-making firms with large accruals now rank at the aggressive end rather than being rewarded by a negative denominator — while preserving the self-normalizing "accrual share of profits" construct that is genuinely absent from the archive. Cumulating over five years also makes both numerator and denominator stable enough that the hurdle reflects accounting style rather than one-year timing noise.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashEarningsGapHurdle
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ib), at), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The most direct evidence that profits are cash-backed is that operating cash flow exceeds reported earnings; a capital-efficient firm whose cash flow runs ahead of its accounting income is reporting conservatively and its profits persist, while one whose earnings run ahead of cash flow has recognized income it has not collected.
evaluated.reasoning: This is the canonical earnings-quality construct and the one channel the archive never tested, because early attempts were rejected for lacking an accruals-exclusive variable — the accrual-capital deflator in the profitability leg now supplies it, so the test is finally admissible. It measures the total earnings-cash wedge from the cash-flow statement rather than reconstructing it from balance-sheet differences, making it free of the acquisition and translation artifacts that contaminate every balance-sheet hurdle at the frontier.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: DiscretionaryTailHurdle
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(TS_MAX(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), MUL(GROWTH(sale, 1), RATIO(LAG(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at))), 1), 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: What discredits a profitable firm is the single worst year of *discretionary* accrual — the largest excess over what its own growth required — because that is the year in which management demonstrably used accounting latitude, and the associated reversal is still working through reported earnings.
evaluated.reasoning: The tail statistic and the expected-accrual benchmark each improved the hurdle separately (worst-year: alpha 4.7% at t 5.11; growth-adjusted: Sharpe 0.542), but applied to the raw accrual the "worst year" partly flags fast growth rather than manipulation, which is precisely the confound the growth benchmark removes — so the combination changes what the tail statistic identifies rather than merely stacking two effects. This is the sharpest available test of whether reversal risk is created by episodes of discretion rather than by chronic accrual levels.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AccrualDecelerationHurdle
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 1), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Tightening of accrual policy is news about future earnings quality: a capital-efficient firm whose accrual intensity fell relative to last year is converting a larger share of each reported dollar into cash than it did before, and because accrual levels are persistent the market anchors on the old regime and underreacts to the improvement.
evaluated.reasoning: Every accrual hurdle in the archive measures a state — level, chronic mean, cumulative sum, worst year, volatility, or growth-adjusted residual — and none measures the *change* in accrual intensity, so this is a new information type rather than a crossing of tested legs. A second-difference hurdle is also close to orthogonal to the persistent characteristics that drive the frontier signals, which is exactly what could add alpha rather than replicate it.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ReversalBufferQuality
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che, lct), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: What makes accrual-based profits dangerous is that their reversal arrives while near-term obligations must still be met; a profitable firm holding cash sufficient to cover its current liabilities can absorb a receivable write-down or inventory markdown without distress, whereas one without that buffer must liquidate accrual assets at a discount and the reversal becomes permanent.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a solvency-of-the-reversal channel rather than an asset-composition channel: cash relative to current *liabilities* asks whether the firm can withstand the unwinding of its accruals, while the archived cash-share hurdle (che/act) asks only what fraction of assets is already realized, and the two order firms very differently for inventory-light, payables-heavy businesses. The related realization channel produced the archive's highest alpha (5.8%), so the buffer interpretation is worth separating from the composition interpretation in the final round.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: BottomLineConversionHurdle
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ib, SUB(revt, cogs)), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Gross profitability is credible only if it survives the journey to the bottom line: a firm whose gross profit is repeatedly consumed by write-offs, impairments, restructuring charges and interest is one whose accrual estimates are being corrected below the operating line, so its headline capital efficiency overstates durable earning power.
evaluated.reasoning: Every hurdle tested so far screens the balance sheet or the cash-flow statement; this screens the *income statement itself*, asking how much of the profitability that qualifies the firm actually reaches shareholders after the charges through which accrual errors are ultimately recognized — a channel absent from the archive and conceptually independent of working-capital measurement. It is also naturally bounded and populated for all firms, so it should not repeat the coverage or tail-instability problems of the cash-flow-statement hurdle.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: PeakBaseProfitQuality
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), TS_MAX(SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 3)), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A firm can flatter profit-per-accrual-capital by managing its balance sheet down at the fiscal year end — factoring receivables, running inventory low, stretching payables into the new year — so the honest capital base is the largest operating-asset base it actually needed over the recent past, and profitability measured against that peak identifies genuinely capital-light earning power.
evaluated.reasoning: This addresses balance-sheet window dressing, a distinct accrual-quality concern that none of the archive's hurdles touch: all prior versions deflate by the single year-end snapshot that management can most easily manipulate, whereas a three-year maximum is invulnerable to a one-year contraction and still slow-moving enough to keep portfolio turnover low. Because it changes what the profitability leg measures rather than re-scaling it, firms whose high ratio comes from a temporarily shrunken base will drop out of the long leg, which is a testable and economically specific prediction rather than a parameter tweak.
evaluated.author: proposer

considered.name: ProfitabilityInCashRegime
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oibdp, at)), INDICATOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), 0))
considered.hypothesis: Profitability is priced correctly (i.e., under-priced) only in the cash-backed accounting regime; when accruals are positive, high reported profitability is partly transitory and earns no premium.
considered.reasoning: The indicator switches the industry-adjusted profitability signal on only for firms with negative total accruals, implementing a regime-conditional rather than continuous interaction. Industry z-scoring removes sector accounting-intensity differences so the switch reflects firm-level earnings quality, not industry membership.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: StableAccrualProfitability
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Durable profitability requires not just low accruals today but a stable accrual process; firms with persistently profitable operations and low-variance accruals have the most credible, least manipulated earnings streams.
considered.reasoning: Accrual volatility is a direct proxy for accounting discretion and estimation error, so interacting smoothed profitability with accrual stability separates firms whose profits are structurally reliable from those whose profits fluctuate with accounting choices. This uses a second-moment accrual concept, which is economically distinct from the accrual-level interactions above.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CashValidatedProfitImprovement
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 1)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Improving profitability is informative about future returns only when the improvement coincides with falling accruals; margin gains accompanied by rising accruals reflect receivable/inventory build-up or accounting timing and reverse.
considered.reasoning: The signal compares the change in profitability against the change in accrual intensity, so it identifies profitability upgrades that are validated by cash conversion rather than by working-capital expansion. Using first differences on both themes captures the dynamic credibility of new earnings news, a distinct mechanism from level-based cash-backed profitability.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CashBackedProfitPersistence
considered.expression: SUMRANK(TS_SUM(MUL(INDICATOR(RATIO(oiadp, at), 0.05), INDICATOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), 0)), 5), RATIO(oancf, at))
considered.hypothesis: What distinguishes durable profitability from soon-to-reverse profitability is the repeated co-occurrence of profitable operations and cash-backed (non-accrual) earnings; a firm that has been simultaneously profitable and low-accrual in many of the last five years has demonstrated a self-financing business model that the market under-extrapolates.
considered.reasoning: The count of years in which both conditions hold jointly is not monotone in either theme's level — a firm with very high profitability financed by accruals scores zero, as does a cash-rich unprofitable firm — so it captures joint history rather than two additive main effects. The second SUMRANK channel only supplies within-count granularity (the count itself takes six values), keeping the persistence interaction as the primary source of cross-sectional variation.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ProfitPerAccrualBloat
considered.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)
considered.hypothesis: Cumulative past accruals are embodied in the stock of net operating assets, so gross profit measured per dollar of accrual-accumulated operating capital separates firms that earn profits on a lean balance sheet from firms whose reported profits rest on a bloated receivable/inventory/net-operating-asset base that must eventually be written down.
considered.reasoning: Unlike a small additive perturbation of total assets, the deflator here is materially different — it strips cash and nets out operating liabilities — so the accrual channel drives large cross-sectional variation rather than acting cosmetically. It converts the accrual theme from a flow to a stock concept (balance-sheet bloat) and asks how much true trading profit that accrual stock supports, which is a distinct mechanism from period accruals.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualRiskAmongProfitable
considered.expression: MUL(NEG(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at))), INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), 0.5))
considered.hypothesis: Accrual quality carries information about future returns mainly where there are strong profits to be validated: among above-median-profitability firms, investors extrapolate reported earnings, so accrual-heavy profits reverse sharply while cash-backed profits persist; among weak-profitability firms accruals carry little extrapolation risk.
considered.reasoning: This is the mirror-image conditioning of the accepted regime signal — accrual quality switched on by the profitability state rather than profitability switched on by the accrual state — so the long and short legs are both profitable firms differing only in cash backing, which is exactly the durable-versus-reversing profit contrast. Deflating accruals by assets and industry-standardizing avoids any division by profit, so loss and near-zero-profit firms are handled without sign scrambling.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CreditSignedProfitability
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), SIGN(NEG(DELTA(wcap, 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Reported operating profitability should be read as good news only when working capital is releasing cash; the same profitability level accompanied by a working-capital build is accrual-financed and mean-reverts, so the accrual sign should flip the interpretation of profits rather than merely shade it.
considered.reasoning: Because the profitability channel enters as a non-negative rank multiplied by a ±1 accrual sign, low-profitability firms are pushed toward zero regardless of accrual state and the extremes are populated only by highly profitable firms separated by cash backing — this is close to a pure interaction rather than a sum of main effects. Using wcap (a dedicated accruals variable) keeps coverage high relative to cash-flow-statement components.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ProfitVsAccrualBloatTrend
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), SIGN(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), at), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: Multi-year accumulation of net operating assets, not the single-year accrual flow, reveals whether a profitable firm is steadily capitalizing costs and stretching working capital; sustained profitability with a shrinking operating-asset base is genuinely cash-generative, while the same profitability with a rising base is accounting-driven and reverses.
considered.reasoning: Replacing the one-year accrual with a three-year trend in the accrual stock tests a slow-moving accounting-aggressiveness state that annual accrual flows measure noisily, while smoothing profitability with MA(·,3) matches the horizon of the credibility question. The sign-conditioning again concentrates the long and short legs among persistently profitable firms, so the spread is an accrual-quality bet, not a profitability bet.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AssetSideAccrualGrossProfit
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), SIGN(ADD(recch, invch)))
considered.hypothesis: Only asset-side accruals (receivables and inventory) indicate that reported margins were manufactured by shipping unsold or uncollected goods; payables and other liability-side items release cash for different reasons, so restricting the accrual conditioner to receivable and inventory changes should sharpen the credibility test on gross margins.
considered.reasoning: The cash-flow-statement components recch and invch measure the receivable/inventory drain directly rather than inferring it from balance-sheet differences contaminated by acquisitions and restatements, giving a cleaner conditioning variable for the "channel stuffing versus real demand" story. Contrasting this with Signal 1 tells us whether accrual composition or aggregate working-capital movement carries the interaction.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: StableWCAccrualProfitability
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), at), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Durable profitability requires a stable accrual process: firms with persistent operating profits whose working-capital accruals have low variance rely little on accounting discretion, so their profits are more informative about future cash flows than equally profitable firms with erratic accruals.
considered.reasoning: This repairs a design the critic accepted but the validator rejected, replacing the shared ib−oancf accrual with an accruals-exclusive working-capital accrual so the second-moment (Dechow–Dichev style) accounting-discretion channel can actually be tested. It is the only proposal in the batch using accrual *instability* rather than accrual level, sign, or trend, so it teaches a distinct lesson about which moment of the accrual process conditions profitability.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: EarningsToAccrualNoise
considered.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3), MA(ABS(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), at)), 5)), 1)
considered.hypothesis: Profitability is credible in proportion to how small the firm's habitual accrual adjustments are: a firm earning steady operating profits while its working capital barely moves is generating cash-validated earnings, whereas the same profit level accompanied by chronically large working-capital swings is largely an accounting-timing artifact that will reverse.
considered.reasoning: Rather than swapping a deflator on an existing profitability ratio, this makes the accrual channel the *scale of measurement error* in earnings, so the return premium is proportional to profitability divided by chronic accrual magnitude — a signal-to-noise construct with no published analogue in either the RNOA or Sloan families. Using mean absolute working-capital accruals over five years (not the current-year signed accrual) captures the firm's accounting style rather than one-year events, and winsorization controls the small-denominator tail.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualGradedProfitability
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Accrual intensity does not merely add to profitability information, it scales it: the higher a firm's profitability, the more its future returns depend on whether those profits were accompanied by large or small balance-sheet accruals, so the accrual measure should enter as a graded multiplier on the profitability signal.
considered.reasoning: The non-negative profitability rank multiplied by a mean-zero, industry-standardized accrual-quality score produces a pure interaction: unprofitable firms are compressed toward zero regardless of accruals, while the long and short tails are both highly profitable firms separated by accrual magnitude — so a positive result cannot be explained by either main effect alone. It also isolates one specific design choice against the accepted sign-conditioned signal: whether graded accrual intensity carries information beyond the mere sign of working-capital accruals.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CashAdjProfitPerAccrualBloat
considered.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oibdp, SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1))), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)
considered.hypothesis: Durable profitability is cash operating profit — reported operating income minus the working-capital accrual that inflated it — measured per dollar of the accrual-accumulated operating capital that had to be tied up to earn it; both the flow and the stock of accruals must be charged against profits.
considered.reasoning: This keeps the deflator that produced the archive's best portfolio alpha but replaces the raw profit numerator with a materially cash-adjusted one (the accrual subtraction is comparable in size to the profit itself, unlike gen-0's trivial denominator perturbation), so the accrual channel now enters twice and in the same economic direction. It tests whether the GP/NOA result strengthens when the numerator is also purged of accrual content, which distinguishes the "accrual bloat" story from a plain profitability-per-capital story.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: GrossProfitGradedByBloat
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: The reason profit-per-accrual-bloat works is an interaction, not a scaling convention: gross profitability is informative about future returns mainly for firms whose operating capital is lean, and nearly uninformative for firms whose balance sheet is inflated by accumulated accruals.
considered.reasoning: This decomposes the archive's best-alpha ratio into an explicit interaction between a non-negative profitability rank and an industry-standardized accrual-stock intensity, so the extremes are populated by profitable firms differing in balance-sheet bloat rather than by mechanical small-denominator cases. If the interaction form reproduces the ratio's alpha, we learn the effect is genuinely conditional; if it does not, the gen-0 result was a deflator effect and future work should stay in ratio space.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: LiabilityStretchGradedProfit
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(apalch, aoloch), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Not all cash backing is high quality: profitable firms whose operating cash flow is supported by stretching payables and other operating liabilities are financing themselves off suppliers rather than converting profits into cash, so their earnings are as fragile as those of receivable-builders.
considered.reasoning: Every prior proposal treated liability-side movements as improving accrual quality (they reduce Sloan accruals) whereas the economics of supplier financing suggest the opposite for profitable firms — this is a genuinely new channel and the first test of whether accrual quality is asymmetric across the asset and liability sides of working capital. Paired with Signal 4 it delivers a clean composition lesson rather than a repeated template.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: UnexpectedAccrualGradedProfit
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), MA(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 5)), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Only the *unexpected* part of accruals signals earnings that will reverse: a growing firm normally accrues working capital every year, so what discredits reported profits is an accrual this year far above the firm's own established accrual norm, which is the symptom of discretionary revenue pulling-forward rather than of business expansion.
considered.reasoning: Rather than rank-wrapping the archived signal, this changes the accrual construct itself from a cross-sectional level to a firm-specific abnormal-accrual deviation from a five-year norm, which is the standard discretionary-accrual identification idea and is economically distinct from Sloan-level accruals. The multiplier remains a signed industry z-score so the conditional sign-flip mechanism is preserved, and because abnormal accruals are far less persistent than accrual levels, the resulting portfolio should reshuffle on genuine accounting-quality news rather than on slow-moving firm characteristics — the plausible reason the level-graded version had a strong slope but a muted FF5 alpha.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CollectionBackedProfitMargin
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(recch, invch), sale), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Under the Compustat decrease-positive convention, positive RECCH+INVCH means receivables and inventory released cash, so profitable firms whose working capital is being collected and sold down have genuinely converted profits into cash, while equally profitable firms whose receivables and inventory absorb cash relative to sales are recognizing revenue ahead of collection and will reverse.
considered.reasoning: The direction is now set by the documented sign convention rather than by back-fitting to the earlier inverted t-stat, and if the archive's inversion was real it will show up here as a clean, interpretable rejection of the convention rather than as a hidden fudge.
