Deflating the receivable/inventory flow by sales rather than assets matches the channel-stuffing mechanism (working capital absorbed per dollar of revenue booked) and makes the conditioner comparable across capital intensities.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: DepreciationBackedProfit
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dpc, at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Firms that still earn strong profits *after* absorbing heavy non-cash depreciation charges are conservatively stated: their accrual accounting subtracts more from reported income than cash economics require, so their earnings are understated and more persistent than those of equally profitable firms carrying negligible non-cash charges.
considered.reasoning: Switching the profitability leg to post-depreciation operating income (oiadp) removes the internal inconsistency: the interaction now identifies firms whose profitability survives the conservative charge, not firms whose EBITDA is flattered by it. Industry standardization of dpc/at absorbs the bulk of the capital-intensity variation in D&A, leaving within-industry differences in depreciation aggressiveness as the conditioning variable, which is precisely the accrual-conservatism concept being tested.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CashProfitPerWorkingCapital
considered.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oibdp, SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1))), SUB(act, che)), 1)
considered.hypothesis: Durable profitability is cash operating profit earned per dollar of non-cash working capital the firm must tie up; receivables and inventory are the accrual assets that both inflate reported profit and consume cash, so profit measured against that accrual stock separates real earning power from accounting-generated profit.
considered.reasoning: The best archive signal used a net-operating-asset deflator that can go negative for net-operating-liability firms, mechanically flipping the ratio's sign for a nontrivial subset; non-cash current assets are strictly non-negative, so this repairs the defect while keeping the cash-adjusted numerator that raised the alpha t-stat from 3.3 to 4.6. Excluding PPE also separates the "accrual bloat" story from the published net-operating-asset/asset-growth anomaly, which was the critic's main identification concern.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: TaxValidatedProfitability
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(pi, at)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(txp, at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Earnings that create a real tax obligation have been validated by a third party with no incentive to accept accrual optimism; among equally profitable firms, those carrying substantial accrued taxes are reporting income the tax authority also recognizes, whereas high book profits with negligible tax accrual are book-only and reverse.
considered.reasoning: Book-tax conformity is an accrual-quality channel completely untested in the archive, and it is conceptually orthogonal to working-capital accruals because it constrains the *income* statement rather than the operating cycle. Pretax income is the correct profitability leg since it is the base on which the tax accrual is computed, making the interaction internally consistent in a way the earlier depreciation proposal was not.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ProfitVsExcessWCGrowth
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(GROWTH(SUB(act, che), 1), GROWTH(sale, 1)), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: The right benchmark for accrual growth is sales growth: a profitable firm whose receivables and inventory grow faster than revenue is granting looser credit or accumulating unsold goods, so its profits are accrual-inflated, while a profitable firm whose working capital grows slower than sales is scaling on real demand.
considered.reasoning: All prior accrual conditioners were deflated by assets, which conflates efficient growth with accrual manipulation; benchmarking working-capital growth against sales growth removes the growth component and leaves the abnormal-accrual component, a normalization never tested in the archive. Because the conditioner is a growth differential rather than a level, it should also carry fresher information than the slow-moving bloat state while remaining economically the same credibility test.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ShortCycleProfitability
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Profits earned with a short (or negative) cash conversion cycle are the most credible: when customers pay before suppliers must be paid, reported profit converts into cash almost immediately and cannot have been manufactured by extending customer credit or stockpiling inventory, whereas the same profit earned with many days of working capital outstanding is accrual-dependent and reverts.
considered.reasoning: The conditioner is net operating working capital expressed in days of sales — a cash-conversion-cycle concept — rather than the one-year accrual flow whose sign the archive has already tested in both directions, so nothing about its outcome is implied by existing results. Deflating by sales instead of assets is also the economically right normalization for an operating-cycle length and separates the idea from the net-operating-asset/asset-growth family the critic flagged.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CashRealizedProfitability
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(che, SUB(act, che)), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Accrual quality shows up in the *composition* of the current asset base, not only in its flow: among equally profitable firms, those whose current assets have been realized into cash have collected their earnings, while those whose current assets sit in receivables and inventory hold profits that are still only accounting claims.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the rescaling exercise with a genuinely different accrual construct — the cash-versus-accrual mix of current assets, a stock-realization measure that no archive signal uses — while keeping the profitability leg bounded so both tails are populated by profitable firms differing in earnings realization. Because the conditioner is a within-current-asset composition ratio rather than an asset-scaled intensity, it is not a restatement of the accrual anomaly or of the NOA anomaly, and its cross-sectional distribution is far better behaved than the unbounded bloat z-score that produced the fmb/alpha divergence.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: PeakProfitAccrualRegime
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5), NEG(ZSCORE(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Profitability at a multi-year high is trustworthy only when the firm's working-capital intensity is simultaneously at a multi-year low; peak profits accompanied by historically elevated receivables and inventory are the classic signature of pulled-forward revenue and revert, while peak profits on a historically lean operating cycle reflect a genuine improvement in earning power.
considered.reasoning: Both legs are measured as positions in the firm's own five-year history, which is a regime concept absent from the archive (all prior signals used cross-sectional levels, one-year flows, or growth differentials) and which directly targets the reversal question the task poses. The profitability leg is a non-negative own-history percentile and the accrual leg a mean-zero cross-sectional standardization of an own-history percentile, so the extremes are firms at profitability peaks separated by whether their accrual intensity is also peaking — a true interaction with no single-ratio delta and no small-denominator differencing.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CumulativeAccrualGradedProfit
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(TS_SUM(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 5), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: What discredits a profitable firm is not the size of its operating asset base per se but how much of that base was built by accruals: five years of accumulated working-capital accruals measures the portion of the balance sheet created by accounting recognition rather than by capital investment, and profits resting on that accumulation are the ones that reverse.
considered.reasoning: This directly addresses the critic's concern that NOA-based conditioners reproduce the published net-operating-asset anomaly: cumulating the accrual flow isolates the accounting-created portion of operating capital while excluding the legitimate installed capital and initial endowment embedded in the NOA level. It also converts the flow family (strong slopes, weak alpha) into a slow-moving state without borrowing the NOA level itself, giving a clean test of which stock definition drives the alpha.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CashAccumulationBackedProfit
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(che, 1), at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: The strongest evidence that reported profits are real is that the cash balance actually grew: profitable firms whose cash stock rises have collected their earnings, whereas equally profitable firms whose cash stock is flat or falling financed the reported profit with accruals or spent it maintaining the operating cycle.
considered.reasoning: Paired with Signal 3 this delivers a clean level-versus-flow lesson within the cash-realization channel — whether it is the accumulated cash position or the current-year cash build that certifies profits — which the archive has never tested. It is also economically distinct from working-capital accruals because cash accumulation is an outcome of the whole operating cycle, not a component of it.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ChronicAccrualGradedProfit
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 3), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Chronic accrual reliance, not a single year's accrual, is what marks profits as unsustainable: a firm that has expanded working capital faster than it collected cash for three consecutive years is systematically recognizing revenue ahead of cash, and its profitability should command no premium.
considered.reasoning: This repairs the archive's most consistent failure mode — flow-graded interactions with strong slopes (fmb 4.7) but negligible alpha (1.5%) — by converting the transient one-year accrual into a persistent three-year accounting-policy state that can sustain a stable long-short portfolio. If the alpha rises while the slope holds, we learn the flow family failed on portfolio persistence rather than on economics, which would redirect the remaining generations toward smoothed flow conditioners.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AbnormalWCDaysProfit
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale), MA(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale), 5)), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Every firm has a structural working-capital cycle determined by its industry and business model; what discredits reported profits is a stretch in receivable and inventory days *relative to the firm's own established cycle*, because that deviation cannot be explained by the operating model and must reflect looser credit terms or unsold output.
considered.reasoning: This is a new conditioning construct rather than a blend: it measures the accrual state as a stock in days of sales (the family that has produced the archive's tradable alphas) but benchmarks it against the firm's own five-year norm (the normalization that has produced the archive's strongest Fama-MacBeth slopes), which is precisely the combination the evidence says is missing. Because the deviation is firm-centered, it also avoids the cross-sectional industry tilt that makes level-based bloat conditioners resemble the published net-operating-asset anomaly.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CumulativeCashBuildProfit
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(DELTA(che, 1), 5), at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Over a full business cycle, genuine profits must eventually show up in the cash box: a firm reporting sustained profitability whose cash balance has accumulated over five years has converted earnings into settled cash, while a persistently "profitable" firm whose cumulative cash build is nil has recycled its reported earnings into accrual assets.
considered.reasoning: This is not a rescaling of the current-asset composition ratio — it is a multi-year cumulative flow, so it distinguishes firms that were always cash-rich (a static balance-sheet type) from firms that actually built cash out of the profits they reported, which is the economically relevant validation. Paired with the accepted one-year cash-build signal it delivers a genuine horizon lesson: whether profit certification requires a single year's cash accretion or a sustained multi-year record.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: WeakestLinkQualityProfit
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Earnings credibility is conjunctive, not additive: a firm qualifies as durably profitable only if it clears both hurdles — high profit per dollar of accrual-accumulated capital *and* no current-year accrual inflation — and failing either one is sufficient to make its profits suspect, regardless of how strong the other looks.
considered.reasoning: A minimum of two industry ranks is a weakest-link aggregation that no archive signal uses and that behaves nothing like an ensemble: averaging lets a strong accrual score rescue weak bloat-adjusted profitability, whereas MIN does not, so the long leg contains only firms credible on both dimensions and the result identifies whether the market prices joint credibility rather than either component. Both inputs are bounded industry percentiles, which should keep the Fama-MacBeth slope and the decile spread reading the same ordering — the divergence that has plagued the unbounded product designs.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: TripleHurdleQualityProfit
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 3), 1))), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che, act), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Durable profitability requires clearing three independent credibility hurdles — high profit per dollar of accrual-accumulated capital, no chronic multi-year accrual reliance, and current assets actually realized into cash — and firms failing any one of them hold earnings that will reverse.
considered.reasoning: Each added hurdle is drawn from an independently validated channel (bloat ratio alpha 4.1%, chronic accrual state alpha 3.4% with Sharpe 0.40, cash realization alpha 5.4%), and because MIN is conjunctive rather than averaging, the third screen removes firms that pass on two dimensions rather than diluting them, which is not achievable by blending. The risk is that a triple minimum concentrates the long leg too narrowly, so the diagnostic value lies in comparing its Sharpe and alpha t-stat against the two-hurdle version.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: WeakestLinkCashRealization
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che, act), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: The two strongest forms of accrual validation are structural (profit earned per dollar of accrual-bloated capital) and realizational (current assets converted into cash); a firm must satisfy both, because capital-efficient profits held entirely in receivables are as suspect as cash-rich firms with no earning power.
considered.reasoning: This substitutes the accrual *stock realization* channel for the accrual *flow* channel inside the winning conjunctive structure, testing whether the weakest-link result depends on the specific flow measure or generalizes across accrual concepts. Because the cash-realization channel previously delivered a 5.4% alpha with a wrong-signed slope, embedding it in bounded ranks also tests whether conjunctive rank construction repairs that divergence.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: WeakestLinkPlainProfit
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: If conjunctive screening is what matters, then requiring plain operating profitability and clean accruals jointly should already capture most of the effect, and the accrual-bloat deflator in the profitability leg is a refinement rather than the source of the result.
considered.reasoning: This decomposes the archive's best signal by stripping the NOA deflator from the profitability hurdle while keeping the conjunctive structure and the accrual hurdle intact, which separates "profitability measured against accrual capital" from "profitability screened by accrual quality." The comparison is essential for interpretation: if performance is preserved, the mechanism is joint credibility screening; if it collapses, the accrual-stock deflator is doing the work and later refinements should target the deflator.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CashBackingConsistencyProfit
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_ZSCORE(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at)), 0), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Consistency of cash backing, not its average magnitude, certifies profits: a firm that has released rather than absorbed working capital in most of the last five years has demonstrated a repeatable cash-generative operating model, whereas the same average accrual achieved through one large swing reveals nothing about durability.
considered.reasoning: A count of cash-backed years is a genuinely new accrual construct here — it is invariant to accrual magnitude and therefore immune to the outlier-driven skew that produced the archive's fmb/alpha divergences, and it distinguishes persistence from average level, which the three- and five-year accrual averages cannot. It also tests the durability hypothesis in its most literal form, asking whether the market underprices a repeated record of converting profits into cash.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: MarginTurnoverWeakestLink
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(sale, SUB(act, che)), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Credible profitability requires both a high margin on what is sold and rapid turnover of the accrual assets used to sell it: a fat margin combined with slow-moving receivables and inventory means revenue is being booked faster than goods move and cash arrives, while fast working-capital turnover on a thin margin is volume without earning power.
considered.reasoning: This is a new economic decomposition rather than an aggregation swap — it splits profitability into the margin dimension and makes the accrual dimension the *turnover velocity of accrual assets*, a quantity no archive signal has used, so neither leg is one of the published anomalies the critic identified. Both legs are bounded industry percentiles and jointly required, the structure that just produced the archive's only signal strong on the cross-sectional slope, the FF5 alpha, and the Sharpe simultaneously.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AbnormalCycleWeakestLink
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale), MA(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale), 5)), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: A firm's profits are durable only if it is efficient in the cross-section *and* undistorted relative to its own history: high profit per dollar of accrual capital certifies the business model, while receivable and inventory days no higher than the firm's own five-year norm certifies that this year's earnings were not manufactured by stretching that model.
considered.reasoning: The two hurdles draw on orthogonal information sets — one cross-sectional and structural, the other firm-centered and time-series — so unlike a pairing of two cross-sectional anomalies this conjunction cannot be a relabeled rank-average of gross profitability and Sloan accruals. Both components have independently delivered alpha with Sharpe near 0.4 (bloat ratio and abnormal working-capital days), and imposing them jointly should raise the alpha t-stat rather than dilute it, which is why this is submitted as a candidate improvement rather than a diagnostic.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: PersistentJointCredibility
considered.expression: TS_MIN(MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 1)))), 3)
considered.hypothesis: Durable profitability means never having failed the credibility test: a firm whose worst joint score over the last three years is still high has been capital-efficient and accrual-clean every year, whereas a firm that clears both hurdles only in the current year may simply be between accrual reversals.
considered.reasoning: This applies the weakest-link logic in a second, orthogonal direction — across time rather than across dimensions — which is a genuinely new construct rather than another channel substitution, and it directly targets the task's durability question by penalizing firms whose credibility is episodic. Because a time-series minimum of a bounded percentile is itself bounded and slow-moving, it should raise portfolio stability and Sharpe relative to the single-year conjunction, whose 0.545 is already the archive high.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ConsistencyHurdleQuality
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at)), 0), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: The frequency with which a firm releases rather than absorbs working capital is a magnitude-invariant measure of cash backing, and profits are durable only when high capital efficiency is combined with a repeated record of cash-backed years.
considered.reasoning: This repairs the archived consistency signal's structural flaw — multiplying a profitability rank by a signed industry z-score inverts the ordering in the low-consistency tail, which is exactly the pathology that produced perverse results in several earlier conditional designs — by re-expressing consistency as a hurdle inside the conjunction. The count is immune to accrual outliers, so if it performs comparably to the winsorized flow hurdle we learn that the priced content of accruals is their sign frequency rather than their magnitude.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CashProfitChronicAccrualHurdle
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oibdp, SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1))), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 3), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: The strongest form of the credibility test uses cash-adjusted profit per dollar of accrual capital as the profitability hurdle and chronic multi-year accrual reliance as the accounting hurdle, so that neither a single clean year nor an accrual-inflated profit level can qualify a firm.
considered.reasoning: Both leg upgrades are independently validated — the cash-adjusted numerator lifted the ratio family's Sharpe to 0.448 and the chronic three-year accrual state lifted the graded family's alpha from 1.5% to 3.4% with Sharpe 0.40 — so combining them inside the conjunctive structure tests whether the refinements are complementary or redundant. Using a smoothed accrual hurdle alongside a cash-adjusted numerator also avoids double-counting the same single-year accrual in both legs, which the current-flow version would do.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CashBuildHurdleQuality
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(DELTA(che, 1), 5), at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Profits are fully validated only when capital-efficient operations are matched by an actual multi-year accumulation of cash, since a firm can look lean on the balance sheet while never converting its reported earnings into a growing cash balance.
considered.reasoning: The five-year cash-build channel produced the archive's second-highest alpha (4.3%, t 4.99) but a zero Fama-MacBeth slope, the classic symptom of an unbounded, skewed multiplier; embedding it as a bounded rank hurdle is the specific repair the bounded-rank evidence prescribes, and it tests whether the alpha survives when the ordering is made regression-readable. It also brings a validation channel independent of working-capital accounting into the conjunctive family, which so far relies almost entirely on working-capital constructs.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: DuPontAccrualTripleHurdle
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale)), MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(sale, SUB(act, che)), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 1)))))
considered.hypothesis: Credible earnings require margin, velocity, and clean accounting simultaneously: a fat margin certifies pricing power, rapid turnover of receivables and inventory certifies that goods actually move and cash actually arrives, and a small working-capital accrual certifies that this year's profit was not created by relaxing either discipline.
considered.reasoning: This decomposes the winning profit-per-accrual-capital ratio into its economically interpretable margin and accrual-asset-velocity components and adds the accrual hurdle, so a strong result identifies which component of capital efficiency the market misprices rather than treating the ratio as a black box. The margin-times-velocity conjunction already delivered fmb 4.39 and alpha 3.1% on its own, so the incremental question is whether the accrual screen adds independent credibility information to a purely operational pair.

considered.name: IntangibleAdjustedQualityHurdle
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(revt, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Accrual accounting distorts profitability in two opposite directions: working-capital accruals inflate reported profits, while the mandatory expensing of R&D deflates them, so the credibility test should compare accrual-clean earnings against a profitability measure that restores the investment accounting understates — R&D-inclusive profit per dollar of accrual-accumulated operating capital.
considered.reasoning: This changes the economic content of the profitability hurdle rather than intersecting two archived winners: every conjunctive signal so far has used unadjusted gross profit or EBITDA, which systematically ranks research-intensive firms as unprofitable even when their accruals are clean and their capital base is lean, so the long leg has been excluding a set of firms the hypothesis says should qualify. Treating unreported R&D as zero is the economically correct convention (firms that do not report the item do not spend on it), and the accrual hurdle is left untouched so the test attributes any improvement specifically to correcting conservative intangible accounting inside the profitability leg.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: IntangibleCapitalQualityHurdle
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(revt, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Consistent intangible accounting requires adding expensed R&D back to profit *and* recognizing the R&D capital stock it created in the denominator; otherwise research-intensive firms are flattered by an artificially small capital base, and the profitability hurdle measures accounting treatment rather than earning power.
considered.reasoning: The numerator-only R&D add-back produced the archive's best cross-sectional slope (6.32) but no alpha gain, which is the signature of a correctly ordered signal whose extreme long leg is contaminated by firms that look efficient only because their intangible investment is unbooked; capitalizing five years of R&D in the denominator removes exactly that contamination. It keeps the two-hurdle structure and the validated accrual hurdle untouched, so any alpha improvement is attributable to the capital-base correction.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: TotalAccrualHurdleQuality
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), dp), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Total accruals — working-capital accruals net of depreciation — are the complete measure of the non-cash component of earnings, so for capital-intensive firms the credibility hurdle should credit the conservative non-cash charge that working-capital accruals alone ignore.
considered.reasoning: The archive's conjunctive family uses only the working-capital component, which systematically flags heavily depreciating firms as accrual-clean regardless of their revenue-recognition behavior and mis-ranks asset-light firms in the opposite direction; including depreciation makes the hurdle the accounting-complete non-cash share of profit. This is the one accrual-definition dimension never varied inside the winning structure, and it directly tests whether the priced content is working-capital manipulation specifically or non-cash earnings generally.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualStabilityHurdleQuality
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(VOL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 1), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Accrual *instability* is an accounting-discretion proxy: a capital-efficient firm whose accruals swing widely from year to year is relying on estimation latitude, so its profits are less informative about future cash flows than those of an equally efficient firm with a smooth accrual process.
considered.reasoning: This repairs a documented failure — the same economics implemented as a product with a signed multiplier delivered alpha −2.3% (t −2.6) in gen 1 — and the archive has since shown that the failure mode was the multiplicative signed structure, not the discretion channel, because recasting other inverted conditioners as bounded hurdles restored them. It is also the only second-moment hurdle in the conjunctive family, so it tests whether credibility depends on the level of accruals or on the reliability of the accrual process.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: WorstYearAccrualHurdle
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(TS_MAX(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 1), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: Accrual credibility is broken by spikes, not by averages: a single year of aggressive working-capital build-up reveals that management will use accrual latitude when needed, and the associated reversal is still working through earnings, so the relevant hurdle is the firm's worst accrual year over the recent past rather than its mean.
considered.reasoning: This is a tail-based accrual construct that is genuinely different from the archive's level, three-year mean, five-year sum, and sign-frequency hurdles, and it is asymmetric where accrual volatility is symmetric — it penalizes only upward spikes while continuing to reward large working-capital releases, which the volatility hurdle in Signal 4 would penalize. Comparing the two identifies whether the market punishes accrual uncertainty per se or specifically the reversal risk created by aggressive years, which is the sharpest remaining question about how accrual quality separates durable from reversing profits.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SelfFundedAccrualBaseQuality
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, SUB(act, che)), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Accrual quality has a financing dimension the archive has never tested: profits earned on a receivable-and-inventory base funded by short-term debt are fragile, because the accrual assets must be refinanced before they convert to cash, whereas the same profits on a self-funded accrual base survive a funding squeeze and do not force fire-sale write-downs of inventory or receivables.
considered.reasoning: This introduces genuinely new economic content into the conjunctive family — how the accrual stock is financed, rather than how large it is, how fast it grows, or how variable it is — using an accruals-menu variable (dlc) that no prior signal has employed. It also gives an independent reason why accrual-heavy profitable firms underperform (refinancing-contingent reversals rather than pure revenue-recognition reversal), so the result discriminates between two distinct explanations of the same archived spread.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ConservativeChargeHurdleQuality
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oiadp, SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(dpc, at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Firms that remain highly profitable per dollar of accrual capital *after* absorbing heavy non-cash depreciation and amortization charges are reporting conservatively: their accrual accounting subtracts more from income than cash economics require, so their earnings understate durable cash flow and are underpriced.
considered.reasoning: The conservatism channel produced one of the archive's strongest cross-sectional slopes (fmb 4.76) but essentially no alpha (0.5%) when implemented as a signed multiplicative z-score, and the archive has repeatedly shown that recasting such channels as bounded rank hurdles inside the conjunction converts slope-only evidence into tradable alpha (the cash-build channel went from a zero slope to 4.0% alpha at t 4.5 under exactly this repair). Measuring profitability after depreciation makes the interaction internally consistent — it identifies firms whose profits survive the conservative charge — which is the specific defect the critic identified in the original conservatism proposal.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SupplierFinancedCycleQuality
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), SUB(act, che)), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Trade credit received is evidence of bargaining power and of a genuinely cash-generative operating cycle: a profitable firm whose receivables and inventory are largely financed by suppliers rather than by its own capital is collecting before it pays, so its profits are cash-backed by construction, whereas a firm carrying its accrual base on its own balance sheet must wait for the cycle to close.
considered.reasoning: The archive established the direction empirically — penalizing operating-liability expansion produced alpha −4.1% (t −2.7), implying liability-side accruals carry the conventional sign — and the complementary short-term-debt version of this financing idea worked as a hurdle (fmb 4.36, alpha 3.8%), but the stock of supplier financing relative to the accrual base it funds has never been tested. It measures a structural competitive-position feature rather than a one-year flow, which is the property that has distinguished the archive's high-Sharpe hurdles from its transient ones.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CashFlowStatementAccrualHurdle
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(recch, ADD(invch, apalch)), at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Working-capital accruals measured directly from the cash-flow statement are free of the acquisition, divestiture, and currency-translation artifacts that contaminate balance-sheet differences, so the credibility hurdle built from reported receivable, inventory and payable cash flows should separate durable from reversing profits more sharply than the balance-sheet accrual.
considered.reasoning: Gens 1–2 produced contradictory evidence on these fields (sign-based fmb −2.17, graded fmb +2.04), leaving the measurement question unresolved; embedding them as a bounded hurdle in the structure that has produced consistent results across every other accrual definition is the cleanest available resolution, with the documented decrease-positive convention fixing the sign a priori. The known cost is coverage (cash-flow-statement items bind at roughly 0.08 versus 0.11), so the result should be judged on alpha t-stat and Sharpe rather than on magnitude alone.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: GrowthAdjustedAccrualHurdle
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), MUL(GROWTH(sale, 1), RATIO(LAG(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at))), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: A growing firm must accrue working capital simply to support its larger sales base, so the credibility hurdle should penalize only the accrual in excess of what the firm's own revenue growth mechanically requires — the residual after subtracting last year's working-capital base scaled up by this year's sales growth is the discretionary part that reverses.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the raw accrual hurdle with a firm-specific expected-accrual benchmark built from the firm's own prior working-capital intensity and realized sales growth, which is new economic content rather than a recombination of two archived legs: every hurdle tested so far penalizes the accrual level, mean, spike, or volatility, none nets out the accrual that growth requires. It should raise both statistics by moving fast-growing but honestly-accruing firms out of the short leg and leaving only discretionary accruers there, which is exactly the population the reversal hypothesis targets.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ProfitFloorAccrualHurdle
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(TS_MIN(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Durable earning power is best evidenced by a floor rather than a level: a firm whose *worst* year of profit per accrual dollar over the last three years is still high has demonstrated that its capital efficiency does not depend on favorable conditions, and combining that floor with current accrual cleanliness identifies profits that are both structurally earned and honestly reported.
considered.reasoning: The tail concept is moved from the accrual hurdle to the profitability hurdle, which is new content: the archive has tested worst-case accruals but never a worst-case profitability floor, and unlike the archived time-minimum of the joint score this keeps the accrual screen contemporaneous so the signal responds to current accounting news while the profitability requirement is structural. That separation also avoids the correlation problem that made the fully time-minimized conjunction weaker than the single-year version.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AssetSideRecognitionHurdle
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), sale), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Revenue recognition is an asset-side act: profits are pulled forward by booking receivables and building inventory, not by managing payables, so the hurdle that screens recognition aggressiveness should measure the increase in non-cash current assets per dollar of revenue and should exclude both the payables offset and the depreciation charge, which reflect financing and capital intensity rather than recognition.
considered.reasoning: This is a different economic object from every accrual hurdle in the archive, all of which net operating liabilities against operating assets and thereby let a payables build-up mask a receivable and inventory build-up of the same size; isolating the asset side makes the hurdle a clean revenue-recognition screen and removes the depreciation-to-sales capital-intensity contamination the critic identified. Scaling by sales is now internally consistent, since both numerator and denominator refer to the same recognition decision.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualShareOfProfitMagnitude
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), dp), 5), TS_SUM(ABS(oibdp), 5)), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Accrual reliance should be judged against the size of the profits it purports to measure: cumulative five-year accruals expressed per dollar of cumulative absolute operating profit measures how much of a firm's reported earning power over a business cycle was accounting recognition rather than cash, and profits with a low accrual share persist.
considered.reasoning: Deflating by the five-year sum of *absolute* operating profit removes the sign-inversion defect the critic identified — the denominator is strictly positive, so weak and loss-making firms with large accruals now rank at the aggressive end rather than being rewarded by a negative denominator — while preserving the self-normalizing "accrual share of profits" construct that is genuinely absent from the archive. Cumulating over five years also makes both numerator and denominator stable enough that the hurdle reflects accounting style rather than one-year timing noise.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CashEarningsGapHurdle
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ib), at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: The most direct evidence that profits are cash-backed is that operating cash flow exceeds reported earnings; a capital-efficient firm whose cash flow runs ahead of its accounting income is reporting conservatively and its profits persist, while one whose earnings run ahead of cash flow has recognized income it has not collected.
considered.reasoning: This is the canonical earnings-quality construct and the one channel the archive never tested, because early attempts were rejected for lacking an accruals-exclusive variable — the accrual-capital deflator in the profitability leg now supplies it, so the test is finally admissible. It measures the total earnings-cash wedge from the cash-flow statement rather than reconstructing it from balance-sheet differences, making it free of the acquisition and translation artifacts that contaminate every balance-sheet hurdle at the frontier.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: DiscretionaryTailHurdle
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(TS_MAX(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), MUL(GROWTH(sale, 1), RATIO(LAG(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at))), 1), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: What discredits a profitable firm is the single worst year of *discretionary* accrual — the largest excess over what its own growth required — because that is the year in which management demonstrably used accounting latitude, and the associated reversal is still working through reported earnings.
considered.reasoning: The tail statistic and the expected-accrual benchmark each improved the hurdle separately (worst-year: alpha 4.7% at t 5.11; growth-adjusted: Sharpe 0.542), but applied to the raw accrual the "worst year" partly flags fast growth rather than manipulation, which is precisely the confound the growth benchmark removes — so the combination changes what the tail statistic identifies rather than merely stacking two effects. This is the sharpest available test of whether reversal risk is created by episodes of discretion rather than by chronic accrual levels.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualDecelerationHurdle
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 1), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Tightening of accrual policy is news about future earnings quality: a capital-efficient firm whose accrual intensity fell relative to last year is converting a larger share of each reported dollar into cash than it did before, and because accrual levels are persistent the market anchors on the old regime and underreacts to the improvement.
considered.reasoning: Every accrual hurdle in the archive measures a state — level, chronic mean, cumulative sum, worst year, volatility, or growth-adjusted residual — and none measures the *change* in accrual intensity, so this is a new information type rather than a crossing of tested legs. A second-difference hurdle is also close to orthogonal to the persistent characteristics that drive the frontier signals, which is exactly what could add alpha rather than replicate it.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ReversalBufferQuality
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che, lct), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: What makes accrual-based profits dangerous is that their reversal arrives while near-term obligations must still be met; a profitable firm holding cash sufficient to cover its current liabilities can absorb a receivable write-down or inventory markdown without distress, whereas one without that buffer must liquidate accrual assets at a discount and the reversal becomes permanent.
considered.reasoning: This is a solvency-of-the-reversal channel rather than an asset-composition channel: cash relative to current *liabilities* asks whether the firm can withstand the unwinding of its accruals, while the archived cash-share hurdle (che/act) asks only what fraction of assets is already realized, and the two order firms very differently for inventory-light, payables-heavy businesses. The related realization channel produced the archive's highest alpha (5.8%), so the buffer interpretation is worth separating from the composition interpretation in the final round.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: BottomLineConversionHurdle
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ib, SUB(revt, cogs)), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Gross profitability is credible only if it survives the journey to the bottom line: a firm whose gross profit is repeatedly consumed by write-offs, impairments, restructuring charges and interest is one whose accrual estimates are being corrected below the operating line, so its headline capital efficiency overstates durable earning power.
considered.reasoning: Every hurdle tested so far screens the balance sheet or the cash-flow statement; this screens the *income statement itself*, asking how much of the profitability that qualifies the firm actually reaches shareholders after the charges through which accrual errors are ultimately recognized — a channel absent from the archive and conceptually independent of working-capital measurement. It is also naturally bounded and populated for all firms, so it should not repeat the coverage or tail-instability problems of the cash-flow-statement hurdle.

considered.name: PeakBaseProfitQuality
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), TS_MAX(SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 3)), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: A firm can flatter profit-per-accrual-capital by managing its balance sheet down at the fiscal year end — factoring receivables, running inventory low, stretching payables into the new year — so the honest capital base is the largest operating-asset base it actually needed over the recent past, and profitability measured against that peak identifies genuinely capital-light earning power.
considered.reasoning: This addresses balance-sheet window dressing, a distinct accrual-quality concern that none of the archive's hurdles touch: all prior versions deflate by the single year-end snapshot that management can most easily manipulate, whereas a three-year maximum is invulnerable to a one-year contraction and still slow-moving enough to keep portfolio turnover low. Because it changes what the profitability leg measures rather than re-scaling it, firms whose high ratio comes from a temporarily shrunken base will drop out of the long leg, which is a testable and economically specific prediction rather than a parameter tweak.

critic_notes.rationale: This is effectively a rank-weighted restatement of cash-based operating profitability (Ball et al. 2016) crossed with the Sloan accrual anomaly, and the stated logic is internally wrong — a product of two positively-signed ranks is monotone in each component, so it preserves both main effects rather than "isolating the joint cell."

Because |ib − oancf| is typically an order of magnitude smaller than total assets, the accrual term perturbs the denominator only trivially, leaving a signal that will be near-perfectly correlated with plain Novy-Marx gross profitability — a known anomaly with a cosmetic adjustment.

The regime-switch construction is a genuine conditional design rather than a repackaged known factor, but it deserves scrutiny because zeroing out all positive-accrual firms piles a large mass at exactly zero (mixing them with median cash-backed firms) and makes the short leg consist of low-profitability negative-accrual firms, an economically odd basket.

This is the Sloan accrual anomaly with the deflator swapped from assets to |operating profit| — the reasoning explicitly denies being a rescaled Sloan measure while computing exactly that — and the absolute-value denominator scrambles interpretation for loss and near-zero-profit firms even after winsorization.

Using the second moment of accruals (an accounting-discretion proxy à la Dechow–Dichev) as the conditioning variable is the most economically distinct idea in this batch, though the 5-period VOL of an annually updated accounting ratio risks being mechanically degenerate or driven by fiscal-year-update artifacts, so the sampling frequency must be verified before the result is believed.

The dynamic "profit improvement validated by cash conversion" framing is coherent and not a standard published anomaly, but the two legs are mechanically near-collinear (Δib/at − Δoancf/at overlaps directly with Δoiadp/at), so the composite may collapse to little more than the change in operating cash flow to assets and should be tested against that benchmark.

The conditional design is internally coherent and does concentrate both legs among profitable firms so it is an accrual-credibility bet rather than a profitability bet, but it hinges entirely on RANK being a non-negative [0,1] percentile — if RANK is demeaned, unprofitable working-capital builders land in the long leg and the sign flips — and SIGN(ΔWC) discards magnitude in a variable that is close to a coin flip year to year.

This is a single-ingredient numerator swap on the archived ProfitPerAccrualBloat expression, i.e. exactly the cosmetic variant the objective warns against, and the resulting quantity is essentially return on net operating assets (RNOA), a long-standing published profitability measure rather than a new cross-theme construct.

The accrual leg is the textbook Sloan (1996) balance-sheet accrual and the profitability leg is standard operating profitability, so the signal is a mechanical equal-weight sum of two of the best-known published anomalies with no genuine interaction — a rank difference is additive, not conditional, so a positive result would teach nothing beyond "both anomalies exist."

Substituting a multi-period trend in the NOA stock for the one-year accrual flow is a defensible slow-moving-accounting-quality state and is the more interesting of the sign-conditioned trio, but it shares the RANK-convention fragility of Signal 1, is structurally the third instance of the same template in this batch, and the NOA-growth conditioner overlaps heavily with the published net-operating-asset/asset-growth anomaly.

The restriction to asset-side accruals is an economically sharper conditioner than aggregate working capital and the sign is correct under the Compustat "decrease (increase)" convention for recch/invch, but the entire result inverts if those fields are stored as raw balance changes, and cash-flow-statement item coverage will likely bind hard on the already-thin sample.

Conditioning profitability on the second moment of the accrual process is the only genuinely distinct lesson in the batch and the accruals-exclusive wcap construction avoids the ib−oancf overlap, though multiplying two non-negative ranks behaves much like an additive composite of two separately-known effects and a 5-period VOL window on annual accruals is a noisy discretion proxy.

Internally consistent and a substantive (not cosmetic) change to the archive's best signal — but it is largely a re-deflated version of the published cash-based operating profitability measure (Ball–Gerakos–Linnainmaa–Nikolaev), and the NOA-style denominator can go negative for net-operating-liability firms, flipping the ratio's sign in a way 1% winsorization will not repair.

A legitimate and diagnostically informative ratio-vs-interaction decomposition whose sign logic checks out, though its cross-sectional ordering will be dominated by the NOA/assets z-score and thus risks largely reproducing the published net-operating-assets anomaly with a profitability tilt.

This is essentially a rank-transform plus industry-neutralization wrapper on the archived AccrualGradedProfitability, and the stated claim that it "holds the economic content fixed" is wrong — replacing a signed z-score multiplier with a non-negative rank eliminates the sign-flip mechanism, converting a conditional interaction into a conjunctive rank product.

Under the actual Compustat convention (RECCH/INVCH are decrease-positive cash-flow items), the expression assigns the *long* leg to profitable firms building receivables and inventory, which directly contradicts the stated hypothesis, and the sign flip is justified only by back-fitting to a single inverted t-stat from the archived sign-based version.

Sign logic is correct under APALCH's increase-positive convention and the asset-vs-liability-side asymmetry in accrual quality is a genuinely new channel, but AOLOCH is a noisy residual grab-bag and this is the fourth instance of the same RANK(oibdp/at)×NEG(IND_ZSCORE(·)) template in the batch.

Internally inconsistent: oibdp is measured *before* depreciation, so multiplying it by D&A intensity systematically favors firms whose EBITDA is high only because their true (post-depreciation) profitability is low, which is the opposite of the "equally profitable but conservative" firms the hypothesis describes — and within-industry D&A/assets is mostly an asset-age/capital-intensity proxy rather than a conservatism proxy.

The deflator swap is defensible on a real mechanical ground (net-operating-asset denominators can go negative and flip the ratio's sign, while act−che cannot), but it remains a fairly incremental re-scaling of the archive's best signal rather than a new mechanism, and act−che near zero for asset-light or financial firms will still create tail instability that 1% winsorization only partly tames.

This is essentially the sign flip of the already-tested LiabilityStretchGradedProfit (whose −4.1% alpha at t=−2.7 mechanically implies roughly +4% here), so the "result" is pre-determined by archive information rather than tested, and the underlying content — liability-side accruals carrying the conventional Sloan sign — is a direct restatement of the published accrual anomaly.

This is a rescaling of GrossProfitGradedByBloat rather than a new mechanism, and its stated logic is internally inconsistent: it claims to hold the firm ordering fixed for the FMB regression while simultaneously claiming to neutralize industry composition, which the final IND_RANK cannot do at once since within-industry ranking necessarily changes the cross-sectional ordering the decile portfolios saw.

The book-tax conformity channel is genuinely absent from the archive and the pretax-income leg is correctly matched to the tax accrual, but txp is a balance-sheet payable — a high stock can equally mean deferred cash outflow, which is a liability-side accrual with the opposite (Sloan) sign — so the mechanism is ambiguous and txp's sparse, lumpy reporting is a real coverage/noise risk.

A one-year change in gross-profit-to-working-capital is close to the long-published Abarbanell-Bushee / Piotroski fundamental signals on changes in margin and asset turnover, it abandons the cross-theme interaction mandate entirely (it is a single-ratio delta), and differencing a ratio with a small, volatile denominator will be dominated by denominator noise.

Benchmarking non-cash working-capital growth against sales growth is a substantively different normalization from the asset-deflated conditioners already tested, the sign logic is internally coherent, and it plausibly separates genuine expansion from accrual inflation — though it overlaps conceptually with Jones-model abnormal accruals, so the novelty rests on the profitability interaction and on growth-rate stability for small-denominator firms.

This is an equal-weight rank ensemble of two already-archived signals (CashAdjProfitPerAccrualBloat and CashRealizedProfitability, the latter with a wrong-signed FMB slope) rather than a new mechanism, so any gain is a portfolio-blending artifact that teaches nothing about which channel is priced, and the shared oibdp/at profitability leg means the components are not as independent as claimed.

The stated logic — isolating the accrual-created portion of operating capital rather than the NOA level — is coherent and does address a real confound with the published net-operating-assets anomaly, but a five-year sum of working-capital accruals is close to five-year NOA growth, so the discriminating power versus GrossProfitGradedByBloat may be smaller than argued.

che/act is a strictly monotone transform of the archived che/(act−che), so this is a cosmetic rescaling of CashRealizedProfitability, and the stated diagnosis is internally inconsistent because the archived version was already winsorized at 1% while this proposal drops winsorization entirely.

The level-versus-flow contrast within the cash-realization channel is a legitimate untested distinction, but Δche is contaminated by financing and investing activity (equity/debt issuance, asset sales), so a positive result would be hard to attribute to earnings validation as the hypothesis requires.

A three-year moving average of an already-tested annual signal is a smoothing variant, not a substantively different construct, and since the underlying ratio is annual the MA mostly adds stale information rather than isolating a persistent state.

Reframing the conditioner from a transient flow to a chronic accrual-policy state is a defensible response to the flow family's strong-slope/weak-alpha pattern, but the three-year mean accrual is nearly the same object as this batch's five-year accrual sum and as the archived ProfitVsAccrualBloatTrend, so the two flow-smoothing proposals are largely redundant with each other.

This is a cosmetic aggregation swap on the archive's best signal that collapses to a plain rank-average of two long-published anomalies (Novy-Marx gross profitability deflated by Hirshleifer-style net operating assets, plus Sloan accruals), so it has diagnostic value at best and essentially no standalone novelty.

The proposal states a positive expected sign while the reasoning openly predicts a materially weaker or negligible spread, which is an internally inconsistent submission of a deliberately-worse variant of an archived signal rather than a candidate expected to improve the joint evidence.

A substantive extension of the conjunctive structure with an economically distinct third screen, though the added cash-realization leg had a wrong-signed Fama-MacBeth slope in the archive and a triple MIN risks concentrating the long leg into a small, unstable, cash-rich subset — so the comparison against the two-hurdle version must be interpreted with coverage in hand.

Substituting the accrual-stock realization channel for the accrual-flow channel inside the winning conjunction is a legitimate generalization test rather than a rediscovery, but it overlaps heavily with the triple-hurdle proposal and inherits the che/act channel's cross-sectional sign divergence, so its incremental information is moderate.

A clean, well-motivated ablation that isolates whether the NOA deflator or the conjunctive screening drives the archive's best result, though the resulting construct — profitability screened by accruals — is itself close to a well-known joint screen and is unlikely to be a novel signal in its own right.

The frequency-of-cash-backed-years count is a genuinely new, magnitude-invariant accrual construct that is not a variant of the archive's level or moving-average accrual conditioners, though the multiplicative industry z-score can turn negative and flip the profitability rank's sign — the same structure that produced perverse results in several archived conditional signals, so the sign behavior in the low-consistency tail should be checked.

This is literally the intersection of two archived winners (WeakestLinkQualityProfit and AbnormalCycleWeakestLink) that share the identical profitability leg, and the archive already showed that adding a third hurdle to the two-hurdle conjunction degrades rather than improves both fmb_tstat and alpha, so it is a cosmetic leg-substitution with little independent information.

Applying the weakest-link operator across time rather than across dimensions is a structurally new construct that is internally consistent (a high three-year minimum of a bounded joint percentile genuinely means "never failed"), with the only caveats being the added history requirement on coverage and its high correlation with the archived single-year conjunction.

The diagnosis of the archived consistency signal is technically correct — multiplying a positive profitability rank by a signed industry z-score inverts the ordering in the negative tail — and recasting sign-frequency as a bounded hurdle is the right repair, though the 0–5 count is coarse and will generate heavy ties inside the MIN.

Both leg upgrades were independently validated in the archive, the expression matches the stated hypothesis with the correct natural sign, and the explicit avoidance of double-counting the same single-year accrual in numerator and hurdle shows the construct was thought through rather than assembled mechanically.

Embedding the cash-build channel as a bounded rank hurdle is a sensible repair and brings a non-working-capital validation channel into the conjunctive family, but the stated diagnosis is somewhat wrong (the archived version was already winsorized and z-scored, so the failure was the signed-multiplier inversion, not unboundedness) and cumulative cash accumulation risks proxying for known cash-holdings/issuance effects.

Decomposing the winning profit-per-accrual-capital ratio into margin and working-capital velocity is a legitimate diagnostic question and the accrual leg is a new combination rather than a rediscovery, but each individual component (gross margin, turnover, working-capital accruals) is a well-known published anomaly and the triple-MIN structure risks the same redundancy that weakened the archived triple hurdle.

This is a genuine internal-consistency fix rather than a cosmetic tweak — the archive's best-slope signal adds R&D to the numerator while leaving the capital base understated, and capitalizing a five-year R&D stock in the denominator is the coherent completion of that adjustment, with a specific and testable diagnosis (long-leg contamination) for why slope improved without alpha improving.

Changing the accrual deflator from total assets to non-cash current assets is a marginal scaling variant of an already-tested hurdle, and the deflator is internally mismatched with the numerator (a net working-capital accrual divided by a gross current-asset base), which also invites instability and outlier-driven ranks in firms with thin working capital.

The Sloan-style total-accrual definition is a legitimate and cleanly motivated accrual-definition test inside the hurdle structure, but the claim that this dimension has never been varied is inaccurate — the same depreciation-inclusive accrual was used in AccrualGradedProfitability and the depreciation channel in DepreciationBackedProfit, both of which produced strong slopes with negligible alpha, so prior evidence already hints this variant will dilute portfolio evidence.

A second-moment hurdle is a substantively different construct and worth one test, but the archive's prior implementation of this exact channel produced an insignificant slope (1.49) alongside significantly negative alpha, and since MIN rewards high stability just as the product did, the failure is more likely directional than structural — the "recast as a hurdle fixes it" argument is asserted rather than evidenced.

This is a mechanical recombination of two already-evaluated legs (the R&D-adjusted profitability numerator and the own-history working-capital-days hurdle, each tested at gen 5–6) with no new economic content beyond "pair the two best components," so its outcome is largely predictable from the existing archive.

A tail/max-based accrual hurdle is genuinely distinct from the level, three-year mean, five-year sum, sign-frequency, and volatility variants, the asymmetry argument (punish spikes, still reward releases) is economically coherent and correctly matched to the expression's sign, and it poses a sharp discriminating test against the volatility hurdle — though its likely high correlation with the existing three-year-mean hurdle caps the expected incremental information.

Despite the framing, this is exactly a top-two blend — the profitability leg is taken verbatim from IntangibleCapitalQualityHurdle and the hurdle leg verbatim from TotalAccrualHurdleQuality, both already measured against the same MIN baseline, so the outcome (~5% alpha, t≈5) is essentially predictable and adds no new economic content.

This is another mechanical cross of two already-tested variants (TotalAccrualHurdleQuality's dp-inclusive definition × WorstYearAccrualHurdle's TS_MAX statistic) on an unchanged profitability leg, and the "worst year" of a dp-inclusive accrual partly ranks firms on low depreciation rather than on aggressive recognition, muddying the stated tail-risk mechanism.

Changing the accrual deflator from assets to sales is a cosmetic normalization variant, and it is internally inconsistent with the hypothesis: the numerator retains −dp, so sales-scaling injects a depreciation-to-sales capital-intensity term that has nothing to do with the revenue-recognition decision the signal claims to screen.

The self-normalizing "accrual share of cumulative profit" idea is genuinely new to the archive, but the denominator TS_SUM(oibdp,5) can be near zero or negative, which inverts the ratio's sign for weak/loss firms and would reward exactly the accrual-inflated firms the hypothesis targets — a defect the MIN structure does not fix, contrary to the stated reasoning.

Trade-credit financing of the operating cycle measured as a stock is a legitimately untested dimension with a direction pre-committed by the archive's liability-side evidence, but the two legs are mechanically entangled (large lct−dlc shrinks the profitability leg's denominator), so the hurdle is only partly independent and the result will need that decomposition check.

A measurement-source robustness test of the accrual hurdle is a reasonable way to resolve the archive's conflicting gen-1/gen-2 evidence, and the sign convention is handled correctly (all three cash-flow items positive = cash released), though it remains a data-definition variant of an existing hurdle whose coverage loss may cap its informativeness.

This is a pure mechanical crossing of two already-tested legs (IntangibleCapitalQualityHurdle's numerator/denominator and GrowthAdjustedAccrualHurdle's residual accrual) with no new economic content, and given both parents already sit at ~0.05 alpha / ~0.55 Sharpe it is a cosmetic consolidation rather than a substantively different hypothesis.

The hurdle recast is internally coherent and correctly signed, but "excess working-capital growth over sales growth" is economically and statistically near-identical to the already-tested GrowthAdjustedAccrualHurdle (which subtracts sales-growth-scaled expected working capital and delivered alpha 0.048, t 4.62), so it is very likely a redundant re-parameterization rather than a new channel.

This is a two-knob parameter tweak of AccrualShareOfProfitMagnitude (5y→3y window, drop dp) justified by a weak diagnosis — a modest alpha alongside a large FMB slope is far more likely a size/breadth or factor-spanning issue than "insufficient portfolio turnover," and a 3-year sum is barely faster-moving than a 5-year one.

(oancf − ib) is essentially the Hribar–Collins cash-flow-statement accrual and thus close to the canonical Sloan anomaly, but it genuinely has not been tested in this archive, uses new fields with far better coverage than the recch/invch/apalch attempt, is correctly signed, and directly addresses the balance-sheet contamination problem flagged at the frontier.

Applying the tail statistic to the growth-benchmarked residual rather than the raw accrual does change what the worst-year screen identifies (discretion versus expansion), which is a defensible non-cosmetic refinement, though it remains a stack of two independently confirmed archive improvements and its incremental information over each parent is likely small.

The stated motivation is unsound — the coverage differences cited come from data requirements (this expression still needs a 5-year xrd sum, so it will not inherit the 0.12 coverage), and dropping PP&E from the base is not a fix for occasionally negative NOA (already winsorized) but a different construct: gross-profit-plus-R&D deflated by a current-asset-only base.
